summary: Production Android now uses gpui-kit =0.11.0 with the exact upstream mobile-host revision 7548ebc4b24f00494af9976af8852c7163ded9ce and a reproducible, minimal compatibility diff. Preparation verifies the diff checksum, upstream revision and complete patched tree without patching shared Cargo sources. Upstream notices, license expressions and the Java IME proxy are preserved; no license was selected and nothing was published.
evidence: Source review: android/patches/gpui-mobile-kit-011.patch changes only four core/renderer pins to 0.3.14 and threads the existing WgpuSurfaceConfig into Android WgpuContext::new (7 additions, 6 deletions). The iOS/dev pins must agree for Cargo resolution; iOS is not verified. The pinned manifest's original text, author credit and license expression are otherwise unchanged. Prepared Java IME proxy and all three upstream license files matched the independently fetched pinned public source hashes.

android/test-prepare-mobile.ps1 passed all six preparation scenarios: fresh public fetch and unchanged replay; refusal of modified worktree, modified index/tree, unexpected files and a changed patch recipe; invalid patch failure with cleanup of only the newly created checkout. All three Android PowerShell scripts parsed successfully. An initial Windows staging-directory rename failure was resolved by preparing in place and validating before returning; negative preparation checks cover cleanup.

cargo metadata --locked --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml --filter-platform x86_64-linux-android --format-version 1 and the locked target dependency tree passed: exactly one Kit 0.11.0, gpui-pre 0.3.14, registry gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.14, WGPU 30.0.2 and local patched gpui-pre-mobile 0.1.0. The upstream vendored renderer is not used. The git revision remains pinned in the application manifest and provenance; the Android lockfile records the path patch.

cargo build --locked --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-linux-android --lib --message-format=json-render-diagnostics passed against the existing production target. Cargo artifacts confirmed wgpu-types debug assertions remain disabled. A separate public-only HEAD archive with only this Android change overlaid, no prototype/private files and a newly fetched host also passed cargo build --locked --offline for the Android library. The lockfile stayed unchanged. Compilation and packaging ran serially, foreground, with temporary files and target output on the development volume.

node scripts/android-kit-frame.mjs passed twice, including after final preparation hardening, on the already booted dedicated Rustday_Edit_X64 x86_64 AVD using its private adb server, host GPU and production GL selection. The ordinary script built and signed the current production APK, observed the ordered board, tapped Review artwork and observed Editing name with that value in the second row's Kit Input while Review sketch remained visible.

node scripts/android-kit-edit.mjs passed twice, including with the final preparation recipe, using only the dedicated rustday_test database. Rejected sign-in left zero sessions; corrected masked input opened the board with one session. The real Kit Input cleared Ink, showed Name required after Save, retained the blank editor, then displayed Coral. System Back hid the IME without saving. Fresh original readbacks before correction and after Back confirmed ordered IDs 42 and 17 at revisions 1/1. Save displayed Coral without the editor; a fresh saved readback confirmed Review sketch/1 and Coral/2 with the same IDs and order.

The business path is unchanged: BoardView owns the draft and stable item ID/revision; EditClient calls the production host off the frame thread; store::rename_item_at_revision owns the committed rename. No application UI, business rule, Java proxy, backend selection or permission behavior was redesigned. Normal gate cleanup exited the host fixture and dropped its schema; package absence and an empty dedicated reverse-mapping list were independently checked. No new build/fixture process remained; pre-existing unrelated processes and the booted AVD were preserved.

cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo fmt --manifest-path android/Cargo.toml -- --check, node --test scripts/run.test.mjs (44/44) and git diff --check passed. Every pre-existing tracked file outside the Android manifest/lock/build script and affected workflow rows retained its initial content hash. No runner gates, verification markers, shared process documents, commits, pushes or PRs were changed by this work. System-volume free space increased rather than being consumed by build output.

Not run: full workspace tests, Clippy, the full packet runner, device-process probe suite, logout/browse/restore/cross-client gates, physical-device or iOS checks, composition/TalkBack, alternate themes and zoom. They are outside this narrowly assigned dependency unification; no new parity claim is made for them. Guide reads used the public GPUI Kit guides when external skill-reference reads were unavailable. Two initial shell invocation/log-capture errors were corrected before the successful locked builds; neither left a build running. Packaging emitted only the existing Java 8 obsolescence warnings. Private artifact pointers are recorded only in the ignored plan.
next: Coordinator review the Android-only compatibility recipe and recorded checks, then reconcile the stale Android version notes in shared architecture/development documents at the permitted milestone boundary.
